projects.title: UMH × Powerhouse demo
projects.abstract: Second companion-software demo from the BD plan: the United Manufacturing Hub supplies machine truth, Powerhouse supplies the promise and the verdict. A purchase-order PDF becomes a frozen commitment, machine evidence accrues against it, and the record closes itself out with a conformance verdict, the internal run cost and the projected contractual exposure. Built unilaterally on UMH's open stack — UMH contributes no work and has made no commitment. The demo is the artefact meant to earn a conversation with them about Powerhouse becoming their integrations partner. Final build: github.com/powerhouse-inc/umh-powerhouse.

deliverables.title: Consultancy partner outreach — week of 31 Aug
Paperless-invoice package refinements — liberuum backlog raised 21 Aug 2026
Simulated UMH factory and Paperless intake, configured
deliverables.description: One compose file brings up the vendored UMH factory demo — machine simulator (4 lines, 13 workcells on OPC-UA and Modbus), umh-core with the UNS and historian bridge, TimescaleDB behind pgbouncer, an nginx gateway — alongside a slim Paperless-ngx. The simulator's fake ERP is switched to manual so it stops minting a competing order every 30 seconds, and the internal cost tables are seeded and served over the costs API.

deliverables.title: Running Powerhouse instance with the production-ledger package
deliverables.description: Switchboard, Connect and PGlite in the same compose, loading umh-production-ledger@0.0.5 from the registry at startup: the v2 pre-ship close-out document model, the ledger editor, the PL Dashboard drive app, the read-only umh-order-poller processor, and the subgraph. An idempotent bootstrap wires the drive, the Paperless document type, the extraction mapping and the webhook.

deliverables.title: Live Paperless to Powerhouse integration with clause-rate extraction
deliverables.description: A purchase-order PDF dropped into Paperless becomes a DRAFT production ledger with the scan attached in roughly 24 to 30 seconds. The model extracts the commitment including the agreement reference and the contract's own clause rates: yield floor, scrap liability per rejected unit, late penalty per hour, OEE floor and how it is evidenced, and the delivery instant with its timezone. The extractor is allowed exactly one operation and can never approve, open, close or sign.

deliverables.title: Commitment freeze and floor-order creation on approval
deliverables.description: A reviewer checks the extraction against the scan side by side, makes the decisions the purchase order does not make (yield floor boundary, production due date, logistics lead time, who must acknowledge), and approves. That one click creates the production order on the floor, binds its id, freezes the commitment against further edits, records every correction with its before and after value, and opens the ledger for evidence.

deliverables.title: Machine evidence and automatic close-out
deliverables.description: Evidence accrues from the floor as append-only snapshots while the run proceeds. When the floor reports the order complete, a processor — not a button — records the close-out: a conformance verdict per promised dimension, the internal run cost with the rates frozen into the record, the projected contractual exposure at the PO's own rates, and a ship-or-hold recommendation published for the shipping process to read. Controlling then acknowledges and the record becomes terminal.

deliverables.title: Demo runbook and presentation materials
deliverables.description: A click-by-click runbook that carries a disclaimer and a real-world fidelity comparison at every step, naming the industry standard each stage stands in for (EDIFACT ORDERS and X12 850, ISA-95, OPC-UA, ISO 22400). Plus a presentation deck, a 16-slide narration script, and a verified account of the five ways the demo still differs from a real deployment.

deliverables.title: Marketing materials — video, posts, landing page
deliverables.description: A full blog draft exists but is not publishable: two of its videos are provisional v1 captures marked do-not-publish, one screenshot is referenced but absent, the evidence-trail capture shows the fabricated 0.0% OEE that v2 removed, five link placeholders are unresolved, and the MCP claim rests on nothing wired into the stack. Also needed: the YouTube recording, the LinkedIn and tweet threads, and an enterprise landing page.

deliverables.title: UMH integration-partner approach
deliverables.description: The demo is the artefact meant to earn the conversation. Decide what UMH sees first — the repos, the blog, or a private walkthrough; identify the right people and the contact path; write the hook covering what we built on their stack and what we are not claiming; define concretely what becoming their integrations partner would mean. Pre-empt the two questions they will ask: why the ledger reads counters instead of the UNS, and who mints the order id.

deliverables.title: Repo and package refinements
deliverables.description: Backlog raised 7 Sep 2026 against the final build. Release correctness: the production-ledger subgraph is undeclared in the manifest though the read API and the stress harness both query it; package.json says 0.0.2 while the demo pins 0.0.5; the publish workflow targets the wrong registry and a lockfile that does not exist; v2 is unmerged on a side branch with no tags; the whole documentation set and stress suite are untracked. Credibility: both repos still document a v1 settlement design the code has not implemented since 3 September, the ten intake stress fixtures have never been run, and umh-actuals-bridge is unregistered so the close-out reports no OEE and no downtime — reading less of UMH's data than UMH itself holds.

deliverables.title: Real-world fidelity reconciliation — close or disclose, per divergence
deliverables.description: A decision gate before UMH sees anything. Five divergences from a real deployment remain, and the existing analysis is partly stale: the priority tables list work that has since shipped, and the document still says the simulator's webhook is off when the build enables it. Re-verify all five, then decide for each whether to close it or disclose it. The open question with the most leverage is whether to stand up a mock ERP: half that path is already live and proven — the simulator posts order events to umh-core's erp-receiver and erp-order-bridge writes them into production_orders, 136 rows including both ledger-created orders — so what is missing is not plumbing but an ERP that mints the order id before approval and sets a production due date, which no order has ever carried. Closing it would fix the one inverted arrow in the demo and make the schedule dimension judgeable. The same call is needed on registering umh-actuals-bridge (today the record holds less about the run than UMH's own historian), the due-date source, and authenticated identity. Output is a written verdict per divergence with its cost, and a runbook whose 'what is real and what is pretend' table matches it.

deliverables.title: Evidence trail filters — show more or fewer parameters
deliverables.description:
The evidence trail is the panel a presenter dwells on longest, and today it is all-or-nothing: a fixed six columns behind a single 'Show all N snapshots' toggle. Runs produce a snapshot per counter change — 327 rows over a two-hour run, 1914 over a twenty-three-hour one — so the table is either collapsed or unreadable. Add a column selector covering the fields the model already stores but never shows (availability, performance, the floor's raw status word, the completion timestamp), let the reader hide columns that are not measured on the current ingest path so the OEE column stops looking like a defect, and add row filtering: a time window, an every-Nth sample, and a scrap-events-only view. The chart series should toggle independently of the table. The default view stays as it is so the demo narration does not change unless the presenter opts in.

Also, based on the parameters selected for the table columns, render the relevant chars accordingly.
